intro.title: Test User Interactions
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple interactive button component and learn how to write tests for user interactions like clicks. You will use React Testing Library to simulate user events and verify that your component responds correctly. The core concept involves writing unit tests that mimic real user behavior to ensure your UI works as expected. You'll use TypeScript for type safety and Jest as the test runner. By the end, you'll be able to test user-driven changes in a React component's state or output.
intro.usecase: Testing user interactions is essential for ensuring that interactive UI components behave correctly in real applications. For example, in e-commerce checkout forms, you need to verify that quantity selectors update totals correctly and that form validation triggers appropriate error messages. In dashboard applications, you must test that filter controls properly update data visualizations and that toggle switches enable/disable features as expected. This practice prevents bugs in critical user flows like authentication modals, data table sorting, or multi-step wizards where incorrect behavior directly impacts user experience and business outcomes.
